subject: Re: Bootstrapping with Poststratification by Species

messages.author: 5900eadecec2d82d
messages.subject: Re: Bootstrapping with Poststratification by Species
parts:
Hi Catherine, (list)

I didn't see a reply to your question on the list - apologies if people=20
have replied off the list and this is duplication.

Firstly, indeed people do sometimes need to assume a common detection=20
function for multiple species. I epxect you've seen the paper by Matt=20
Alldredge on this, giving advice on possible approaches to doing the=20
lumping.

Alldredge, M., K.H. Pollock, T. S. & Shriner, S. 2007 Multiple-species=20
analysis of point count data: a more parsimonious modeling framework
Journal of Applied Ecology 44:281=96290

Secondly, if you are interested in estimates by species and by site,=20
then I don't understand why you are obtaining density estimates at the=20
point level. Distance can't cope with multiple levels of stratificatin,=20
so you can't do the natural thing of having stratum for species and=20
substratum for site, or some such. But since you're only interested in=20
estimated by species and site then why not combine the two into one set=20
of strata and import data into Distance this way. So, for example, if=20
you have 2 species and 3 sites, you would create a column in your data=20
spreadsheet for species_site that would have 6 levels (sp1site1,=20
sp2site1, sp1site2, etc). Import this as the stratum label. Area is=20
the area of the stratum; lines are repeated within in each stratum.=20
Then, as Distance to produce stratum estimates of variance, but not=20
global estimates.

With this setup you can use Distance to do the bootstrap model averaging.

Hope this helps,

- Len

--=20
